body:
## Problem

When `fieldPaths` or `customCallbacks` are non-empty, `processContext` runs only
field-path/callback processing plus `dataTypeMasker->applyToContext`, never `recursiveMask`
over the remaining context values.

## Evidence

With an email pattern + a `password => remove` fieldPath,
`{note: "mail me at john@example.com"}` passes through unmasked; it masks correctly when no
fieldPaths are set.

## Impact

Adding a single field rule disables all regex masking of every other context value —
a GDPR data leak.

## Fix

In the fieldPaths/callbacks branch, run each not-yet-processed field through
`recursiveProcessor->recursiveMask()` as the no-fieldPaths branch does.
Status note: Pre-existing defect, not introduced by PR #115. Behavioral fix + new tests
belong in a dedicated PR, not the PHP-upgrade branch.

## Resolution
DataTypeMasker::processFieldValue now routes strings with no data-type mask through the recursive/regex masker, so configuring a fieldPath no longer disables pattern masking. Test: MaskingBypassRegressionTest::testFieldPathConfigDoesNotDisableRegexMaskingOfOtherFields
title: Regex masking silently skipped for context fields when any fieldPath/callback is configured

body:
## Problem

`processArrayValue` calls `dataTypeMasker->applyMasking`; with `array => 'recursive'`
configured, `maskArray` re-enters `recursiveMaskCallback($value, 0)`, resetting depth to 0 at
every level, so `maxDepth` never trips.

## Evidence

200k-deep nested array with `['array' => 'recursive']` → PHP segmentation fault
(exit 139) in PoC.

## Impact

Remote-triggerable crash from attacker-controlled log context.

## Fix

Thread the real current depth into the recursive-array mask (`$currentDepth + 1`);
enforce `maxDepth` on that path.
Status note: Pre-existing; same dedicated-PR scoping as NP-001.

## Resolution
applyMasking()/maskArray() now take the caller's depth and recurse at currentDepth+1 instead of 0; RecursiveProcessor::processArrayValue passes it. Test: testRecursiveArrayMaskCannotBypassDepthGuard
title: Depth guard bypassable via DataTypeMasker 'recursive' → segfault on deep arrays

body:
## Problem

12 of the 24 patterns in `DefaultPatterns::get()` are anchored with `^`/`$`, so they only
match when the subject string *is* the whole value. Applied to a log **message** — the
library's headline use case — they never fire. Affected: US SSN, IBAN (both), phone, email,
DOB (both), passport, credit-card test numbers, Bearer token, API key, MAC.

## Evidence

With `patterns: DefaultPatterns::get()`, `GdprProcessor::maskMessage()`:

    'user john.doe@example.com logged in'   -> UNMASKED
    'called +358 40 1234567 today'          -> UNMASKED
    'paid to FI21 1234 5600 0007 85 ok'     -> UNMASKED
    'auth Bearer abcdefghijklmnop123 ok'    -> UNMASKED
    'born 1985-03-12 in Turku'              -> UNMASKED
    'passport A123456 issued'               -> UNMASKED

The same values as whole context field values mask correctly
(`{"email":"***EMAIL***"}`), which is why the existing tests pass — every default-pattern
test asserts against a bare value, never against an embedded one.

## Impact

Email addresses, phone numbers, IBANs, dates of birth, passport numbers and bearer tokens
pass through unmasked in log messages while README.md:402-413 documents them as covered.
A GDPR data leak in the library's primary advertised path.

## Fix

Drop `^`/`$` from the patterns that describe substrings and use `\b` boundaries instead
(as the already-unanchored HETU/IPv4/vehicle/EHIC patterns do). Add a test asserting each
default pattern masks its value **embedded in a sentence**, not only standalone — that test
is what would have caught this.

## Resolution
DefaultPatterns rewritten: 11 of 12 anchored patterns now use \b boundaries (generic API-key heuristic stays anchored by design). Tests: testDefaultPatternsMaskValuesEmbeddedInAMessage (9 cases), testGenericApiKeyHeuristicDoesNotMaskOrdinaryMessageText
title: Half the default patterns are anchored and never match inside log messages

body:
## Problem

Ten default patterns carry the `/u` modifier. When the subject contains a malformed UTF-8
byte, PCRE aborts with `PREG_BAD_UTF8_ERROR` and `preg_replace()` returns `null`. Both
masking paths treat that as "leave the value as-is", so the unmasked original is emitted.

## Evidence

`$bad = "\xC3\x28";` (invalid sequence), patterns = `DefaultPatterns::get()`:

    maskMessage("card 4111111111111111 ssn 123-45-6789 raw={$bad} end")
      control (valid UTF-8) -> "card ***CC*** ssn ***MEDICARE*** end"
      with bad byte         -> "card 4111111111111111 ssn 123-45-6789 raw=\303( end"
      preg_last_error_msg() == "Malformed UTF-8 characters, possibly incorrectly encoded"

Via the wired `__invoke()` path the card leaks in both message and context:
`{"note":"card 4111111111111111 ..."}`.

## Impact

Malformed UTF-8 is routine in real logs (truncated multibyte, latin-1 payloads, binary
blobs). Any record carrying one silently bypasses masking of every `/u` pattern. Silent
unless an `auditLogger` is configured; `MaskingOrchestrator` logs `preg_replace_error` only
in that case, and `GdprProcessor::maskMessage()` likewise.

## Fix

Before applying `/u` patterns, coerce the subject to valid UTF-8 rather than passing it
through — e.g. `mb_convert_encoding($v, 'UTF-8', 'UTF-8')` or
`mb_scrub()` — and re-run. Treat a remaining `PREG_BAD_UTF8_ERROR` as fail-**closed**
(replace the whole value with the mask) instead of returning the original, since the
library cannot prove the value is PII-free.

## Resolution
MaskingOrchestrator::applyPatterns retries on PREG_BAD_UTF8_ERROR against an mb_scrub()'d subject and logs malformed_utf8_scrubbed, instead of returning the value unmasked. Test: testMalformedUtf8DoesNotDisableMasking
title: A single invalid UTF-8 byte disables masking and leaks PII

body:
## Problem

`GdprProcessor::maskMessage()` passes the full pattern list to a single
`preg_replace($keys, $values, $value)`. PCRE returns `null` for the **entire** call if any
one pattern errors, so the method returns `$value` completely unmasked — every other
pattern's masking is lost with it.

## Evidence

`src/GdprProcessor.php:208`: `$result = preg_replace($keys, $values, $value);` then
`if ($result === null) { ...; return $value; }`. Demonstrated by the invalid-UTF-8 case:
one failing `/u` pattern drops masking for the non-failing credit-card and SSN patterns
too. `MaskingOrchestrator::maskMessageWithJsonSupport()` (lines 213-230) does the same job
in a per-pattern loop and correctly skips only the failing pattern.

## Impact

All-or-nothing masking on a public API method: the blast radius of one bad pattern is every
pattern.

## Fix

Replace the batch call with the per-pattern loop `MaskingOrchestrator` already uses, so a
failing pattern is skipped and logged while the rest still apply. Add a test with one good
and one erroring pattern asserting the good pattern still masks.

## Resolution
GdprProcessor::maskMessage now delegates to MaskingOrchestrator::applyPatterns (per-pattern loop); the batched preg_replace is gone. Test: testFailingPatternDoesNotVoidOtherPatterns
title: maskMessage() batches all patterns, so one failing pattern voids every mask

body:
## Problem

Unanchored broad patterns are evaluated before narrower ones and swallow their matches, so
values are masked under the wrong label and two patterns can never fire.

## Evidence

With `patterns: DefaultPatterns::get()`:

    'ssn is 123-45-6789 here'      -> 'ssn is ***MEDICARE*** here'   (expected ***USSSN***)
    'nic 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E up'     -> 'nic ***IPv6*** up'            (expected ***MAC***)

`MASK_MEDICARE` `/\b\d{3}[-\s]\d{2}[-\s]\d{4}\b/` is structurally identical to a US
SSN; `'***IPv6***'` `/\b[0-9a-fA-F]{1,4}:[0-9a-fA-F:]{7,35}\b/` matches any MAC address.
The US-SSN and MAC patterns are additionally anchored, so they cannot win even on a bare
value in message context.

## Impact

Audit trails and mask labels misreport which data class was found — a compliance-reporting
defect. The MAC and US-SSN patterns are effectively dead code.

## Fix

Order specific patterns before general ones in `DefaultPatterns::get()` (the README already
advises this at line 419 — the defaults do not follow it), and tighten the IPv6 pattern to
require at least one group of 4 hex digits or an `::` so it stops matching MAC addresses.
Add tests asserting the *label*, not merely that masking occurred.

## Resolution
DefaultPatterns reordered specific-before-general: US SSN precedes Medicare, MAC precedes IPv6. Verified by the labelled assertions in testDefaultPatternsMaskValuesEmbeddedInAMessage
title: Default pattern collisions mislabel data and make two patterns dead

body:
## Problem

the test API-key value at tests/GdprDefaultPatternsTest.php:130 (15-char
suffix) matches only the generic
`[A-Za-z0-9\-_]{20,}` alternation, never the `sk_(live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}` branch; any
string matching the `sk_` branch is always matched by the generic branch first.

## Evidence

Length analysis of the alternations; no test exercises the `sk_` branch.

## Impact

Dead pattern branch that suggests coverage which does not exist.

## Fix

Test both alternations separately, or remove the shadowed `sk_` branch and document.

## Resolution
The shadowed sk_ alternation was split out into its own unanchored pattern /\bsk_(?:live|test)_[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}\b/, and the generic 20+ heuristic kept anchored. Both branches are now reachable and independently testable
title: `sk_` API-key pattern alternation is shadowed and untestable

body:
## Problem

`MASK_REGEX` configs store `pattern::replacement`, but `ContextProcessor::maskValue`
applies only the processor's global patterns and never reads
`getRegexPattern()/getReplacement()`. Only `FieldPathMaskingStrategy` honors it, and that
class is not wired into `GdprProcessor`.

## Evidence

`{card: 'card 1234'}` with `regexMask('/\d+/', 'NUM')` and no global patterns is
returned unchanged.

## Impact

Users believe a field is masked when it is not.

## Fix

In `maskValue`, when the config has a regex pattern, apply it directly via
`preg_replace`.
Status note: Pre-existing; dedicated-PR scope.

## Resolution
ContextProcessor::applyRegexMask now reads FieldMaskConfig::getRegexPattern()/getReplacement() and applies them via preg_replace, falling back to the processor-wide patterns only when no per-field pattern is set. Verified: regexMask('/\d{4}$/','XXXX') on "1234-5678" -> "1234-XXXX"
title: FieldMaskConfig::regexMask() custom pattern/replacement ignored by main processor

body:
## Problem

The MASK_REGEX branch does `(string) $value` on arrays.

## Evidence

`{user: ['email' => 'a@b.com']}` with a MASK_REGEX fieldPath emits an
"Array to string conversion" warning and stores the literal `'Array'`.

## Impact

Nested data destroyed; masking intent silently lost.

## Fix

Recurse into arrays (or `json_encode`) before applying regex, matching
`AbstractMaskingStrategy::valueToString`.
Status note: Pre-existing; dedicated-PR scope.

## Resolution
applyRegexMask JSON-encodes arrays/objects instead of (string)-casting, so an array field no longer becomes the literal "Array". Verified: ["a"=>"secret"] -> {"a":"***"}
title: Array field value under MASK_REGEX stringified to literal "Array"

body:
## Problem

`maskValue` invokes `customCallbacks[$path]` with no try/catch (only
`processCustomCallbacks` is guarded).

## Evidence

A path present in both `fieldPaths` and `customCallbacks` with a throwing callback
propagates out of `__invoke`.

## Impact

Log record lost; app may crash inside the logger.

## Fix

Wrap the callback invocation in `maskValue` in try/catch mirroring
`processCustomCallbacks`.
Status note: Pre-existing; dedicated-PR scope.

## Resolution
The customCallback branch of maskValue() is now wrapped in try/catch mirroring processCustomCallbacks(); the error is sanitised and audit-logged. Verified: a throwing callback no longer aborts the record
title: Throwing callback registered via fieldPaths escapes and aborts logging

body:
## Problem

`processContext` calls `maskFieldPaths` (which prefers the customCallback) and then
`processCustomCallbacks` (which runs it again).

## Evidence

PoC shows callback invoked twice (`H(H(bob))`).

## Impact

Non-idempotent callbacks double-apply; audit logs duplicate.

## Fix

Process each path once; skip already-handled paths in `processCustomCallbacks`.
Status note: Pre-existing; dedicated-PR scope.

## Resolution
processCustomCallbacks() now takes the paths maskFieldPaths() already handled and skips them, so a path configured in both places runs its callback once. Verified: callback ran 1x
title: Callback runs twice when a path is in both customCallbacks and fieldPaths

body:
## Problem

Two gating CI steps fail on the current tree, so `ci.yml` cannot pass on a PR to `main`.

## Evidence

Run at HEAD (5e861ea) on PHP 8.4.23 with the committed `composer.lock`:

    ./vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G --no-progress  -> exit 1
    ./vendor/bin/rector --dry-run --no-progress-bar               -> exit 2
    ./vendor/bin/psalm                                            -> exit 0
    ./vendor/bin/phpcs                                            -> exit 0

PHPStan's single error:
`tests/RegressionTests/SecurityRegressionTest.php:282 — Parameter $context of class
Monolog\LogRecord constructor expects array<mixed>, string given (argument.type)`.
Root cause at lines 259-266: `$current = &$deepNesting;` then `$current = 'deep_value';`
widens the inferred type of `$deepNesting` to include `string`.

Rector would change 4 files: `config/gdpr.php:1`, `examples/conditional-masking.php:1`,
`src/Strategies/RegexMaskingStrategy.php:246`, `src/Strategies/StrategyManager.php:180`
(missing closure param/return types picked up by `AddArrayAnyAllClosureParamTypeRector`
and `AddArrowFunctionReturnTypeRector`).

## Impact

Every PR is blocked by a pre-existing failure unrelated to its own change, which trains
reviewers to ignore red CI. CLAUDE.md declares a zero-tolerance, exit-code-0 policy that
the tree currently violates.

## Fix

Break the reference before reassigning in the test so the array type stays `array`:
`unset($current); $deepNesting[...]['level'] = 'deep_value';` — or assign through a fresh
variable. Then run `composer lint:fix` to apply the four Rector changes.

## Resolution
Fixed the reference reassignment in SecurityRegressionTest (store payload as an entry, then unset the reference) and applied the 4 Rector changes. All four gates now exit 0: phpstan, rector, phpcs, psalm
title: CI lint gate is red at HEAD: PHPStan exits 1 and Rector exits 2

body:
## Problem

Blindly `preg_replace`s the first N `[]` occurrences in encoded JSON, counting `{}`
in the raw original, with no structural awareness.

## Evidence

`{"a":"x[]y","b":{}}` → `{"a":"x{}y","b":[]}` — the `[]` inside a string value was
rewritten and the genuine empty object emitted as `[]`.

## Impact

Any log payload containing `[]`/`{}` inside string values is silently mutated.

## Fix

Decode with `json_decode($json, false)` to preserve empty-object identity instead of
regex surgery on encoded output.
Status note: Pre-existing; dedicated-PR scope.

## Resolution
encodePreservingEmptyObjects now rebuilds object-vs-array identity structurally via restoreObjectShape(), comparing against json_decode($originalJson, false) instead of rewriting the first N '[]' occurrences in the encoded output. fixEmptyObjects() kept but marked @deprecated (public API). Tests: testJsonMaskingPreservesStructureWithoutCorruptingStrings (4 cases incl. '[]' inside a string value)
title: JsonMasker::fixEmptyObjects corrupts string contents

body:
## Problem

If `PatternValidator::validateAll()` stops rejecting a catastrophic-backtracking
pattern, the test calls `error_log()` and `assertTrue(true)`; the catch-all
`assertInstanceOf(Throwable::class, $e)` is tautological.

## Evidence

Patterns like `/^(?=.*a)(?=.*b)(.*)+$/` are covered nowhere else; a validator
regression ships silently.

## Impact

The DoS-protection promise of a GDPR library is untested.

## Fix

Data provider asserting `InvalidRegexPatternException` per rejected pattern; separate
expected-accept test for tolerated patterns (mirror the fix applied to
CriticalBugRegressionTest in NP-031).

## Resolution
redosProtectionRejectsCatastrophicBacktrackingPatterns is now a DataProvider test with expectException(InvalidRegexPatternException) per pattern. All 11 patterns verified genuinely rejected, so acceptance now fails the test instead of calling error_log() and assertTrue(true). The catch-all assertInstanceOf(Throwable) is gone.
title: ReDoS security regression test cannot fail on a ReDoS regression

body:
## Problem

Vehicle plates, UK NI, CA SIN, UK bank, CA bank, Medicare, EHIC, and IPv6 masks
have no test anywhere.

## Evidence

`grep -ri 'MASK_VEHICLE|MASK_UKNI|MASK_MEDICARE|MASK_EHIC|medicare|IPv6' tests/`
returns no hits.

## Impact

A regex typo in any of them leaks unmasked PII with no failing test.

## Fix

Extend GdprDefaultPatternsTest with one positive and one negative case per default
pattern. New coverage may surface real pattern bugs — schedule with the dedicated fix PR.

## Resolution
Added testPreviouslyUncoveredDefaultPatternsMaskAndDoNotOvermatch: 9 data-provider cases (vehicle x2, UK NI, CA SIN, UK bank, CA bank, Medicare, EHIC, IPv6), each asserting the value masks under the expected label AND that a near-miss stays untouched. 9/9 pass.
title: Eight default GDPR patterns have zero test coverage

body:
## Problem

For each malicious pattern, both "constructor accepts" (`assertTrue(true)`) and
"constructor throws" (tautological assertInstanceOf) pass.

## Evidence

Test cannot fail regardless of validation behavior.

## Impact

Injection-style patterns reaching production config are never caught here.

## Fix

Split into expected-reject / expected-accept lists with explicit assertions.

## Resolution
Split into inputValidationRejectsMaliciousPatterns (5 patterns, expectException(GdprProcessorException)) and inputValidationAcceptsPatternsWithInlineComments. Verified empirically which patterns the constructor rejects; /(?#comment).*(?#)/ is legitimately accepted and is now pinned separately rather than hidden behind an either-outcome-passes loop.
title: Security tests accept every outcome (malicious-pattern constructor test)

## Problem

The caught value is a Throwable by definition.

## Evidence

Assertion can never fail.

## Impact

Masks which exception types are actually acceptable.

## Fix

Assert the specific expected exception class(es); rethrow unexpected ones.
Status note: The CriticalBugRegressionTest occurrence was removed by NP-031's fix; the
remaining sites belong with the NP-006/NP-013 test restructuring.

## Resolution
All 4 tautological assertInstanceOf(Throwable::class) sites removed: 2 replaced by expectException data-provider tests, 1 narrowed to GdprProcessorException in ComprehensiveValidationTest, 1 deleted in CriticalBugRegressionTest after PHPStan proved it a dead catch (catch.neverThrown). grep now reports 0 occurrences.
title: Tautological assertInstanceOf(Throwable) in catch blocks

## Evidence

Two full test runs per event with two different consumers (Codecov vs
artifact+PR comment).

## Impact

Merge into one workflow; run tests once, feed both consumers from the same coverage.xml.

body:
## Problem

`fail_ci_if_error: false` plus secret token means missing/rotated CODECOV_TOKEN
silently skips upload forever.

## Evidence

Config as written.

## Impact

Coverage tracking dies silently.

## Fix

`fail_ci_if_error: true` for push events, or alert on upload failure.

## Resolution
Codecov upload now sets fail_ci_if_error: true, so a missing or rotated CODECOV_TOKEN fails the job instead of silently skipping the upload forever.
title: Codecov upload failures invisible

body:
## Problem

The repository has no secret-scanning step and no `.gitleaks.toml`. Adopting one now would
start from 22 pre-existing hits, all synthetic.

## Evidence

`grep -rl 'gitleaks|trufflehog|detect-secrets' .github/ .pre-commit-config.yaml` -> no match.
pre-commit provides only `detect-private-key`. `gitleaks detect` over 130 commits reports
`leaks found: 22`, e.g. `tests/RegressionTests/SecurityRegressionTest.php:165` and `:222`,
rule `stripe-access-token`. Inspection confirms these are deliberate fixtures —
`'API key invalid: sk_live_abc123def456ghi789'`, `'password=secret123'`,
`'super_secret_jwt_key_2024'` — used to assert that `SecuritySanitizer` redacts them. No
real credential was found.

## Impact

A genuinely leaked credential would not be caught by any automated gate. This matters more
than usual here: a GDPR-masking library is the kind of dependency whose compromise is
high-value.

## Fix

Add a `gitleaks` pre-commit hook (or a CI step) plus a `.gitleaks.toml` whose allowlist
scopes those fixture paths, so the baseline is clean and any new hit is real.

## Resolution
Added .gitleaks.toml (allowlisting tests/ and docs/audit/ fixture credentials) and a gitleaks pre-commit hook. Repo scan now reports 'no leaks found' (was 22). Verified detection is preserved: a stripe-format key planted in src/ is still caught with this config.
title: No secret scanning in CI, and no allowlist for the 22 known test fixtures

body:
## Problem

`docker/Dockerfile` correctly creates and switches to a non-root `developer` user and Trivy
reports 0 misconfigurations for it. Two smaller gaps remain.

## Evidence

`docker/Dockerfile:1` `FROM php:8.5-cli-alpine` and line 12
`COPY --from=composer:2 /usr/bin/composer` — both mutable tags, so a rebuild can silently
pick up a different base than CI validated. `docker/docker-compose.yml:20` runs
`image: php:8.5-cli-alpine` directly rather than the built image, so that service runs as
root without the `developer` user or the tuned php.ini.

The only HIGH findings Trivy reports are in `vendor/guuzen/psalm-enum-plugin/Dockerfile`
(DS-0002 root user, DS-0029 missing `--no-install-recommends`) — a vendored dev dependency's
own file, not shipped and not this project's to fix.

## Impact

Non-reproducible local builds, and a compose service whose runtime user differs from the
documented one.

## Fix

Pin both bases by digest (`php:8.5-cli-alpine@sha256:...`, `composer:2@sha256:...`) and let
Renovate bump them — `.github/renovate.json` already manages the rest. Point the
compose service at the built image, or add `user: "1000:1000"` to it.

## Resolution
docker-compose php85 service now runs as user 1000:1000 instead of root, matching the Dockerfile's developer uid/gid.
title: Container base images are floating tags; one compose service bypasses the non-root user

body:
## Problem

The playground updates result panels via JavaScript with no ARIA status semantics, so a
screen-reader user gets no indication that pressing a button produced output.

## Evidence

`demo/templates/playground.html` (478 lines): `aria-*` attribute count 0, `role=` count 0.
It has `lang=` on `<html>`, six `<h2>` headings, and 2 `<label>`s for its 2 form controls
(those are fine). The 6 `<button>`s write into result containers that carry no
`aria-live`/`role="status"`.

## Impact

WCAG 2.2 AA 4.1.3 (Status Messages) failure. Scope is the optional demo page only — the
library itself has no UI.

## Fix

Add `role="status" aria-live="polite"` to the `#results` and `#auditLog` containers, and
`aria-atomic="true"` so the whole updated result is read rather than the diff.

## Resolution
Added role=status + aria-live=polite (+aria-atomic) to all dynamically-written result containers in demo/templates/playground.html (maskedOutput, matchesOutput, auditLog, defaultPatterns, fullResults) and demo/index.php. WCAG 2.2 AA 4.1.3 addressed.
title: Demo playground results are not announced to assistive technology

body:
## Problem

Two defects in the shipped demo endpoint (`php -S localhost:8080 demo/index.php`):
(a) `testPatterns()` treats a failed `preg_replace` as a no-op, returning the **original**
text under the `masked` key with an empty `errors` array; (b) `testProcessor()` returns
`$e->getMessage()` verbatim to the HTTP client although the library ships
`SecuritySanitizer::sanitizeErrorMessage()` for exactly this.

## Evidence

(a) `demo/PatternTester.php:52-55` — `$result = @preg_replace(...); if ($result !== null)
{ $masked = $result; }`. Probe with `/^(a+)+$/` against 40 `a`s:

    demo testPatterns: 0.005s, errors=[], preg_last_error_msg()="Backtrack limit exhausted"

The response claims success and shows unmasked text. (`preg_match_all` failing is likewise
ignored at line 47.) Note the backtrack limit caps runtime at ~5 ms, so this is a
correctness bug, not a DoS.

(b) `$t->testProcessor('hi', [], ['/[unclosed/' => 'X'])` returns
`["Invalid regex pattern '/[unclosed/': Invalid regex pattern syntax [Context: pattern:
\"/[unclosed/\", reason: ..., pcre_error: 0, ...]"]`.

`testPatterns()` also never calls `PatternValidator`, which the library provides and which
correctly rejects `/^(a+)+$/` with `InvalidRegexPatternException`.

## Impact

A demo whose stated purpose is verifying masking silently shows a false "masked" result —
the worst possible failure mode for this tool. Raw exception text leaks internal paths and
config to whoever hosts the playground.

## Fix

In `testPatterns()`, check the return of `preg_match_all`/`preg_replace` and push
`preg_last_error_msg()` into `errors` instead of silently keeping the original; route
patterns through `PatternValidator` first. In `testProcessor()`/`testStrategies()`, wrap
`$e->getMessage()` in `SecuritySanitizer::sanitizeErrorMessage()`.

## Resolution
testPatterns() now validates via PatternValidator::isValid, checks preg_match_all/preg_replace return values and reports preg_last_error_msg() into errors instead of silently returning unmasked text as 'masked'. testProcessor()/testStrategies() wrap exception messages in SecuritySanitizer::sanitizeErrorMessage().
title: Demo playground reports unmasked text as masked and echoes raw exception messages

body:
## Problem

CLAUDE.md states "INFO-level issues are NOT acceptable" and "Exit code must be 0". CI runs
`./vendor/bin/psalm --show-info=true`, which *prints* INFO issues but still exits 0, so the
declared policy is not enforced by anything.

## Evidence

    ./vendor/bin/psalm --no-cache --no-progress --show-info=true  -> exit 0
    INFO issue breakdown: 101 x DeprecatedMethod

All 101 are `PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase::expectExceptionMessage` marked deprecated in
PHPUnit 13 (e.g. `tests/Strategies/StrategyEdgeCasesTest.php:53`,
`tests/Streaming/StreamingProcessorTest.php:154`). PHPUnit itself separately reports
9 deprecations across 142 tests, including
`PatternValidator::clearCache() is deprecated, Use instance method clearInstanceCache()`
at `tests/InputValidation/GdprProcessorValidationTest.php:33`.

## Impact

A stated zero-tolerance rule that no gate checks drifts silently; the INFO count grows
unnoticed until a PHPUnit major removes the deprecated method and the suite breaks.

## Fix

Either enforce the policy — add `--show-info=true` together with a non-zero threshold
(Psalm `errorLevel` / `--error-level`, or grep the output and fail the step) — or amend
CLAUDE.md to say INFO is advisory. Then migrate the 101 call sites to
`expectExceptionMessageMatches()` and switch `clearCache()` to `clearInstanceCache()`.

## Resolution
Psalm INFO count 101 -> 0. All 131 expectExceptionMessage() calls renamed to expectExceptionMessageIsOrContains() (the exact method the deprecated one delegates to, so semantics are unchanged); the 2 remaining DeprecatedMethod hits are JsonMaskerEnhancedTest deliberately covering the deprecated fixEmptyObjects(), suppressed with a documented class-level annotation. ci.yml now greps the psalm report for '^INFO:' and exits 1, so the zero-INFO policy is actually enforced. Note: 9 PHPUnit runtime deprecations remain by design - 50 test call sites deliberately exercise the deprecated PatternValidator static API.
title: Psalm INFO gate is unenforceable: 101 INFO issues while the step exits 0

body:
## Problem

`tests/PerformanceBenchmarkTest.php` asserts on wall-clock timings and absolute memory
figures. These pass or fail with machine load rather than with code correctness, so the
suite is intermittently red for reasons unrelated to any change.

## Evidence

`testPatternCachingEffectiveness` compared run 2 against run 3 of the same loop and required
under 20% variation. Eight consecutive runs on one machine, unchanged code:

    run1 FAIL 25.5%   run2 OK   run3 FAIL 34.8%   run4 OK
    run5 FAIL 47.6%   run6 OK   run7 FAIL 20.1%   run8 OK

It also did not test caching at all: `PatternValidator`'s static cache API
(`cachePatterns`, `isValid`, `getCache`) has **zero callers in `src/`**, so no amount of
masking populated the cache the test was named after. Two `microtime(true)` return values
at lines 196 and 201 were discarded unused.

`testConcurrentProcessingSimulation` failed once in a full-suite run and passed in isolation
and in three subsequent full runs — same class of flake.

Seven absolute thresholds remain in the file, e.g.
`assertLessThan(5.0, $avgTimePerOperation, ...)` (line 89),
`assertLessThan(1.0, $timePerItem, ...)` (line 181),
`assertLessThan(50, $memoryUsed, ...)` (line 261).

## Impact

A flaky suite trains maintainers to re-run CI rather than read failures, which is how a real
regression gets waved through. The risk is concrete here: correcting the default patterns
made masking do more work, and the timing assertion started failing about half the time —
a correct fix looked like a test failure.

## Fix

`testPatternCachingEffectiveness` has been rewritten to assert the caching behaviour
directly (cache populated once, re-validation served from cache, invalid patterns cached as
invalid) and is now deterministic across repeated runs. Do the same for the remaining
thresholds: assert algorithmic properties (operation counts, cache hits, peak-memory
proportionality between input sizes) rather than absolute milliseconds, or move the
benchmarks into a separate non-gating suite.

## Resolution
Removed the scaling-ratio assertion (times[i]/times[0] divided by a sub-millisecond baseline - the proven flake) and replaced it with an algorithmic assertion that all 15 records come back fully masked. Remaining wall-clock thresholds loosened to pathology-catching ceilings (5ms->50ms/op, 1ms->25ms/item, 100ms->2s); memory bounds kept as-is since they are stable. Perf suite ran 4/4 green, assertions up from ~5 to 242.
title: Performance suite asserts on wall-clock timings, making CI intermittently red

body:
## Problem

`PatternValidator::$validPatternCache` is a static array keyed by the raw pattern string,
written on every validation and never evicted or size-capped.

## Evidence

`src/PatternValidator.php:243-251`:

    if (isset(self::$validPatternCache[$pattern])) { return self::$validPatternCache[$pattern]; }
    ...
    self::$validPatternCache[$pattern] = $isValid;

The only reset is the explicit `clearCache()` at line 232 — itself deprecated in favour of
`clearInstanceCache()`, and called from tests only.

## Impact

Harmless under PHP-FPM, where the process dies per request. In a long-running worker
(Octane, RoadRunner, Swoole) that validates caller-supplied patterns, the cache grows
without bound for the worker's lifetime. Note `RateLimiter::$requests` and
`RateLimiter::$lastCleanup` are static too, so per-request state is shared across every
request a worker handles — same class of assumption.

## Fix

Cap the cache (e.g. drop the oldest entries past ~1000) or key it on an instance rather
than statically. Document in README that the static caches assume a
request-per-process model, or reset them from a worker-tick hook.

## Resolution
Both caches bounded by PatternValidator::MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES (1000) via a shared rememberIn() helper that drops the oldest half on overflow. Applies to the instance cache (validate()) and the static one (isValid()).
title: Unbounded static pattern cache grows for the process lifetime

body:
## Problem

Only prove no exception; silent acceptance of bad config still passes.

## Evidence

A validator that accepts-and-mangles input passes all of these.

## Impact

For validators guarding masking config, silent acceptance means unmasked data
downstream.

## Fix

Assert observable outcomes, or use an explicit `assertNoException`-style helper.

## Resolution
All 15 assertTrue(true) calls removed and replaced with expectNotToPerformAssertions() plus a comment naming the contract (void validator: passing means not throwing). Verified each of the 15 methods had no other assertion, so the conversion is exact. Rejection behaviour is already covered by the matching negative tests in the same classes. grep for assertTrue(true) now returns 0.
title: 16+ assertTrue(true) "does not throw" tests assert nothing observable

body:
## Problem

Dozens of `@psalm-return 'plugin-1'`-style docblocks on trivial anonymous-class
methods; several place `#[\Override]` before the docblock, detaching it in some tools.

## Evidence

Diff of PR #115.

## Impact

Docblocks desynchronize on the next value change and bury real diffs.

## Fix

Drop literal `@psalm-return` docblocks on test doubles; rely on native return types.

## Resolution
All 40 literal @psalm-return 'literal' docblocks removed from anonymous test doubles across 9 files; the native return types carry the same information. psalm still exits 0 with 0 INFO afterwards. The finding's second claim - that some sites place #[\\Override] before the docblock, detaching it - did not reproduce: every occurrence had the docblock first, which is correct.
title: Generated literal-type docblocks on test doubles add churn

## Problem

PR #115 extracted `$this->testPlugin` into setUp() but ~10 tests still define
identical inline anonymous-class plugins.

## Evidence

e.g. PluginAwareProcessorTest lines 463+, 609+, 622+.

## Impact

Duplicated fixtures drift independently.

## Fix

Finish the extraction; parameterize only where a custom hook is needed.

## Resolution
Added TestHelpers::namedPlugin($name) and replaced the 11 getName-only inline anonymous plugins across the 3 builder test files with it; the 3 files now use the TestHelpers trait. The other 13 anonymous plugins were left alone - inspection showed each overrides a distinct hook (preProcessMessage, postProcessContext, getPatterns, priorities), which is exactly the 'parameterize only where a custom hook is needed' case the finding allows. Also added the missing @param on TestHelpers::createAuditLogger, which PHPStan surfaced once more classes used the trait.
title: Partial setUp() extraction leaves duplicated inline plugin fixtures

body:
## Problem

Public "@api" subsystems are parallel implementations not referenced by the core
pipeline; `FieldPathMaskingStrategy` handles custom regex correctly while the wired
`ContextProcessor` does not (NP-003).

## Evidence

Grep shows no references from the core pipeline.

## Impact

Two masking paths drift; correct behavior exists but is unreachable.

## Fix

Consolidate onto one masking path, or add cross-tests asserting identical output.

## Resolution
Added tests/RegressionTests/MaskingPathParityTest.php: 10 cases asserting GdprProcessor and StrategyManager+RegexMaskingStrategy produce identical output for the default patterns and for a custom pattern. Both paths currently agree, so the drift that produced NP-003 is now pinned and will fail here first. Full consolidation onto one masking path is deliberately NOT done - it is an architectural change beyond this audit.
title: Strategy layer not wired into GdprProcessor (drift source)

body:
## Problem

Whole public subsystems are defined, documented with `@api` and tested, but never reached
from the library's own pipeline. This is the concrete extent of the drift NP-016 names.

## Evidence

Reference count from anywhere in `src/` excluding each class's own file:

    StrategyManager          -> 0
    StreamingProcessor       -> 0
    SerializedDataProcessor  -> 0
    KAnonymizer              -> 0
    RegexMaskingStrategy     -> 1  (only src/Strategies/StrategyManager.php)
    FieldPathMaskingStrategy -> 1  (only src/Strategies/StrategyManager.php)

`src/` carries 51 `@api` annotations. The strategy subtree is self-referential: the only
consumer of the strategies is `StrategyManager`, which itself has no consumer. The only
production caller of any of it is `demo/PatternTester.php::testStrategies()`.

## Impact

Two implementations of the same behavior drift apart and only one is wired — proven by
NP-003, where `FieldPathMaskingStrategy` honors a custom `FieldMaskConfig` regex and the
wired `ContextProcessor` silently ignores it. Users following the `@api` docs get the
unwired path's behavior, which no integration test covers.

## Fix

Decide per subsystem: wire it into `GdprProcessor` (making the strategy layer the single
masking path), or move it out of `@api` and document it as an optional standalone
component. If both paths must coexist, add cross-tests asserting
`GdprProcessor` and `StrategyManager` produce identical output for the same input.

## Resolution
Documented the four caller-less subsystems in a new README 'Standalone Components' section as supported building blocks the user wires up, rather than pipeline internals, and pointed at the parity test as the GdprProcessor/StrategyManager contract. README also now documents the boundary-anchoring and specific-before-general ordering the DefaultPatterns fix introduced.
title: Four public subsystems have zero callers anywhere in src/

body:
## Problem

(a) `illuminate/*: "*"` with `minimum-stability: dev` tests a moving target;
(b) pr-lint has `contents/actions/issues: write` for a lint job; (c) stale.yml carries
unused top-level perms and a caller-less `workflow_call`; (d) psalm.xml/phpstan.neon carry
~25/~30 blanket suppressions while CLAUDE.md declares zero-tolerance.

## Evidence

Config as written.

## Impact

Larger attack/drift surface; policy and config contradict each other.

## Fix

Constrain illuminate majors; trim workflow perms; document the suppressions as approved
exceptions or burn them down.


## Status 2026-07-30

Partially fixed:

- (a) DONE — `illuminate/console|contracts|http` constrained from `"*"` to
  `"^12.0 || ^13.0"`; `composer validate` passes and the lock re-resolves unchanged
  (illuminate 13.23.0).
- (c) DONE — `stale.yml` top-level `permissions:` replaced with `permissions: {}`
  (deny-by-default); the job block already grants what it needs. The caller-less
  `workflow_call` trigger was left in place: it may serve an external caller not
  visible from this repository.
- (b) OPEN — `pr-lint.yml` grants `actions: write`, `contents: write`, `issues: write`.
  The job's only step is the third-party `ivuorinen/actions/pr-lint` composite action,
  whose required scopes cannot be verified from this repository, and trimming them
  blind risks breaking a working workflow. Needs a check against that action's
  definition.
- (d) OPEN — psalm.xml / phpstan.neon suppressions not yet triaged.

## Resolution
(a) illuminate/console|contracts|http constrained from '*' to '^12.0 || ^13.0'; composer validate passes, lock re-resolves unchanged. (b) pr-lint.yml trimmed from 6 scopes to 4: cloned ivuorinen/actions and confirmed contents/pull-requests are documented as required, statuses is required by GITHUB_STATUS_REPORTER: true in .mega-linter.yml, packages: read for the ghcr image pull; actions: write and issues: write dropped - nothing in the action touches those APIs. actionlint + yamllint pass. (c) stale.yml top-level permissions replaced with permissions: {} (deny-by-default); caller-less workflow_call left in place as it may serve an external caller. (d) Suppressions triaged by evidence: phpstan ignoreErrors 42 -> 18 (24 removed as never-matched, verified via reportUnmatchedIgnoredErrors which is now left ON so dead ones cannot re-accumulate); psalm issueHandlers 22 -> 9 (13 removed as producing zero issues at errorLevel 5, verified by flipping every suppress to error), each survivor now annotated with its actual issue count.
title: Dependency and permission hygiene (grouped)

body:
## Problem

The original message is returned when the masked result is empty or `'0'`.

## Evidence

Pattern `/secret-\d+/ => ''` leaves `secret-123` fully unmasked.

## Impact

Legitimate redaction-to-empty leaks the sensitive original.

## Fix

Track whether a replacement occurred (e.g. `preg_replace` count) instead of inferring
from the result string.
Status note: Pre-existing; dedicated-PR scope.


## Status 2026-07-30

Attempted and reverted. Removing the `'' || '0'` guard in
`MaskingOrchestrator::regExpMessage()` fails six tests that pin the current behaviour
as intended:

- GdprProcessorComprehensiveTest::testRegExpMessagePreservesOriginalWhenResultIsZero
- GdprProcessorConditionalRulesTest::testRegExpMessageReturnsOriginalWhenResultIsEmpty
- GdprProcessorConditionalRulesTest::testRegExpMessageReturnsOriginalWhenResultIsZero
- GdprProcessorExtendedTest::regExpMessagePreservesOriginalWhenMaskingResultsInEmpty
- GdprProcessorTest::testRegExpMessageReturnsOriginalIfResultIsEmptyString
- GdprProcessorTest::testRegExpMessageReturnsOriginalIfResultIsStringZero

Since `applyPatterns()` only assigns when `$count > 0`, a final result of `''` means a
pattern genuinely replaced the content with `''` — so returning the original re-emits
unmasked text (e.g. `'/^\d{16}$/' => ''` on a bare card number returns the card).
That reads as a leak, but flipping it reverses six explicitly-written assertions, so it
is a product decision rather than a mechanical fix. **Needs a maintainer call before the
tests are rewritten.**

## Resolution
Maintainer confirmed the guard is a leak. Removed the '' || '0' fallback from MaskingOrchestrator::regExpMessage(); the masked result is now returned as-is. Safe because applyPatterns() only adopts a replacement when preg_replace reported a match, so an empty result means a pattern deliberately masked the content. Rewrote the 6 tests that pinned the old behaviour to assert the corrected outcome, and added MaskingBypassRegressionTest::testFullyRedactedMessageIsNotReplacedByTheOriginal proving a card number masked to '' no longer comes back.
title: Message masking discarded if the masked result is '' or '0'
